answer: Convex ingress pricing at the wharf: each agent session reserves kernel-scheduling capacity, priced by a basalt-rooted attestation of concurrent sessions per physical host. The curve is p(n)=c·n^1.7, so spawning n sybils on one host costs O(n^2.7) total while honest low-concurrency agents pay near c. Reservations release on clean exit, but sybil bursts lock capital and scheduler quota, making mass identity creation superlinear rather than gated.
